Tony Binda (25) and Colin Pearson locked in battle in the Wimbledon Cup. For the winner, see the sparkling report elsewhere in this issue.
GERRY NORTH finishes a fine run on stage 5 to hand over to COLIN PEARSON in second place, only 4 seconds behind the leaders, Reading.
Bottom left: Cross country Vice-Captain - Gene Vincent, sorry, Colin Pearson.
The Belgrave trio of John Stow (27), Colin Pearson (24) and Tony Fairclough (18) plough their way through the Surrey County Cross County Championship and help take the team to 2nd place.
Back Page: Colin Pearson (7) and Clive Shippen (4) reach 'splashdown' during the Surrey County Championship Steeplechase. They finished 4th and 5th respectively.
Top: Pete Carton (right) wins the 800 metres from Colin Pearson, both recording the same time.
Back Cover: At last! Colin Pearson wins his first ever Club Championship, the 800 metres, from Alan Mead and Pete Carton.
Bottom left: Colin Pearson (32) and Simon Lloyd (27) fight it out at the half way mark. Colin got the better of it on this occasion but Simon had his revenge at the 'Southern'.

The 10,000 metre championship for the "Tom Carter" Cup. Top left: Lionel Mann leads the main bunch - Brian Gorman, Paul Roche, Leo Coy and Jamie Stevenson. Top centre: Charlie Manning attempts to hold on to Martin Best. Top right: Second-placer Colin Pearson. Bottom left: A rare appearance on the track for Stuart Masterson, here leading Keith Duckett and junior Richard Dorman. Bottom right: Steve Williams, who in his first season of track athletics has raced over all distances from 200 to 10,000 metres.
Left. Colin Pearson, off 140 metres, chased by Simon Holmes, Jim Rimmer the back marker, and marathon man John Davies.

Some interesting styles in baton changing at the 100 x 1 mile relay.
Top left. Kevin Clarke (83) demonstrates the cross leg shuffle as he takes the baton from new member L.Lyons.
Top right. M.Harrison (13) demonstrates the walkers change as he hands over to P.Moysey.
Bottom left. Steve Webb (69) milkman to the last gives Pat Lyttle no change.
Centre. Ian Morton (75) provides a fine example of the jumping high level pass with Graham Allerton intercepting.
Bottom right. Colin Pearson (84) uses the jumping low level pass to send Tony Fairclough on his way.
